chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Habib al-Khath'ami, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man has wealth with him as a deposit; may he take from it without the permission of its owner? He said: “He must not take, unless he has the means to repay.”

And he said: I said: What do you think—if he finds someone who guarantees it for him, while he does not have the means to repay, and the one who guarantees him bears witness against himself, may he take from it? He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.أَشْهَدَ: caused to testify or formally witnessed
key_terms.وَدِيعَةً: property entrusted to someone for safekeeping; a deposit
key_terms.وَفَاءٌ: the ability or means to repay and fulfill the liability
key_terms.يَضْمَنُهُ: guarantees it; undertakes liability for repayment

ai.seo_question: Can someone use wealth left with him as a deposit without the owner's permission?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning property held as a deposit. It states that one may not take from deposited wealth without the owner's permission unless he has the means to repay it, or a valid guarantor assumes responsibility for repayment. The narration emphasizes protection of entrusted property and financial responsibility.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4090 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Habib al-Khath'ami, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man who has wealth in his possession as a deposit (wadi'ah). Can he take from it without the owner's permission?
Imam (as) said: "He should not take from it unless he has the means to repay it."

I then asked: "What if he finds someone who guarantees it for him, but he himself does not have the means to repay, and he has the guarantor testify on his behalf, can he take from it?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes."
